config.scope: Q1 decision layer formalization and repair. Reads the existing official Q1 inference artifacts only; no retraining of the delivered model, no change to features, folds, probabilities or the legacy integer-median grade column. Fixes the calibration leakage and card hierarchy violations reported in docs/审查问题清单_46ca932_20261027.md items 1 and 3.
config.task: Replace the legacy integer conditional median (which never emits 5/6) with a non-forced cumulative-probability top-k rule, cap children by their card parent, and estimate the panel-mean calibration strictly nested inside every outer-training set.

target_universe.note: Aroma and Flavour acetaldehyde slots exist in the 52-column paper table but carry no label or official probability; they stay NA and are excluded here.

decision_rule.name: non_forced_cumulative_probability_topk
decision_rule.group_size: n = number of cells of that target in that outer fold
decision_rule.training_rate_ge5: mean(panel_weighted_median >= 5) over the other folds of the same target
decision_rule.training_rate_6: mean(panel_weighted_median >= 6) over the other folds of the same target
decision_rule.k5: round_half_even(training_rate_ge5 * n), clipped to [0, n]; 0 means the target/fold emits no grade 5
decision_rule.k6: round_half_even(training_rate_6 * n), clipped to [0, n]; 0 means the target/fold emits no grade 6
decision_rule.assignment_order: 1) promote the top-k6 cells by probability_rating_6 to grade 6; 2) among the remaining cells promote the top-k5 by probability_rating_ge5 to grade 5; 3) every other cell keeps min(legacy_integer_median, 4)
decision_rule.tie_break: descending probability, then ascending row position inside the group (independent of the sort implementation)
decision_rule.why_non_forced: Only 34/50 targets have any observed panel median >= 5 and 12/50 any = 6; forcing a 5/6 on every target (force>=1 variant) destroyed precision and panel-median MAE, so promotion is rate-calibrated per target and fold.

parent_child_cap.parent_rule: parent target id = first two underscore-separated segments of the child target id + '_all' (e.g. A_malt_grain -> A_malt_all)
parent_child_cap.operation: deterministic post-processing: grade[beer, child] = min(grade[beer, child], grade[beer, parent]) for every beer and every pair
parent_child_cap.ordering: parents are '_all' aggregate targets that are never themselves children, so one pass over the pairs is final; pairs are sorted by child column index for determinism
parent_child_cap.rationale: the paper card defines a child check box as 0 or equal to its parent, so the frozen table must satisfy child <= parent on every cell

calibration.leak_fix: strict nesting: for every outer fold, the calibrator is fitted on inner-fold OOF predictions produced by refitting the official raw-panel model on the outer-training beers only (two inner folds, make_splits seed = 20261024 + 100 + outer_fold). The outer-validation labels are never read by any feature or parameter.
calibration.inner_fold_definition: outputs/r2_raw_q1_20261026/rating_weights_and_folds.csv outer_fold is the outer split; inner splits use beer_models.baseline.make_splits on tasting_category_fine within each outer-training set, protocol seed 20261024 + 100 + outer_fold, 2 folds

methods.nested_linear: per (target, outer fold) OLS of panel_weighted_mean on the inner OOF integer median, fit on the inner cells of the outer-training beers
methods.nested_isotonic: per (target, outer fold) isotonic non-decreasing fit of panel_weighted_mean on the inner OOF integer median (numpy PAVA in q1_decision), clipped outside knots; constant-score folds fall back to the training mean
methods.nested_style_linear: per (target, outer fold) OLS of panel_weighted_mean on [inner OOF integer median, style mean]; the style mean is the outer-training mean panel_weighted_mean per tasting_category_fine from 1.csv, unseen styles fall back to the outer-training global mean
methods.nested_quantile: per (target, outer fold) marginal calibration mapping each outer integer median to its mid-rank among inner OOF medians, then to the inner empirical panel_weighted_median quantile at that level (method='lower')

calibration.rounding_for_grade_like_metrics: numpy.rint (ties to even) then clip to [0, 6]
calibration.voided_pre_fix_numbers: The 2026-10-28 hand-off calibration rows (fold-wise linear 0.5027213833, style 0.4622337899, isotonic 0.5025975663, quantile 0.6502882443) were produced with the leaky one-level scheme and are NOT reported as results; they are kept only as a reference in summary.json under voided_pre_leakfix_calibration_reference.

metrics.macro_spearman: per-target Spearman between prediction and panel_weighted_mean for targets with at least 3 distinct reference values, then nanmean (not computed for the calibration rows)
metrics.high_grade: truth = panel_weighted_median >= threshold; prediction = grade >= threshold; precision/recall are cell-level panel metrics, not per-taster accuracy
metrics.individual_weighted: raw 0-6 records from the external anonymized sensory table, weighted by weight_within_beer (total weight 12500); this is the legacy evaluand and is reported only as a contrast
metrics.lower_bound: panel_median_oracle_individual_level: predict the observed panel-weighted median for every cell and score it against the weighted raw records; this is the L1 information floor of the cell-identity-only predictor, not a model
metrics.calibers: q1__metric_calibers.csv reports four disjoint definitions per prediction set: exact5 (prediction == 5 vs panel median == 5), exact6 (prediction == 6 vs panel median == 6), ge5 (prediction >= 5 vs panel median >= 5) at beer level, plus the same definitions weighted over the per-taster raw records. n_predicted/true_positive/precision/n_observed/recall are cell counts (beer level) or weight mass (individual level). The previously published '204 cells, 25.49% precision, 26.26% recall' is the ge5 caliber with 188 grade-5 cells plus 16 grade-6 cells, not an exact-5 metric.

outputs.q1__submission_wide_250x50.csv: beer rows sorted ascending, 50 target columns sorted ascending
outputs.verification.json: assertions against experiments/lead_review/q1/decision_topk_report.json (pre-cap table), the parent/child cap, the leakage perturbation test and the legacy hand-off columns
outputs.summary.json: key numbers including leakage and hierarchy before/after

column_semantics.q1__high_grade_coverage_by_target.csv: n_predicted_ge5 / n_predicted_6 are the pre-cap top-k decision stage expected by the frozen delivery contract; n_predicted_*_parent_capped describe the official parent-capped submission table (q1__submission_long_12500.csv)
column_semantics.q1__metrics_summary.csv: method=q1_topk_nonforced is the pre-cap stage (0.408 / 204 >=5 / 16 six); method=q1_topk_nonforced_parent_capped is the official capped stage (0.40648 / 194 >=5 / 14 six); never mix the two

verification.handoff_semantics: only the legacy columns (integer median, panel references, probabilities, fold) are expected to match the pre-fix hand-off; the new grade column, the calibrated panel mean and the metrics summary are leak-free recomputations and are recorded as diverging, not silently mixed
verification.non_forced_evidence: grade 5 count 188 < 198 observed and grade 6 count 16 < 19 observed; at least one (target, fold) has k5 = 0 and at least one has k6 = 0

metric_row_semantics.q1_topk_nonforced: non-forced cumulative-probability top-k decision BEFORE the parent/child cap; this is the row consumed by the frozen delivery contract (src/beer_models/delivery_current.py) and it reproduces the audited prototype (0.408, 204 cells >=5, 16 cells 6)
metric_row_semantics.q1_topk_nonforced_parent_capped: OFFICIAL submission grades: the same top-k decision followed by the deterministic child<=parent cap for the 24 checkbox rule pairs (0.40648, 194 cells >=5, 14 cells 6)
metric_row_semantics.rule: the two rows are different stages of one pipeline; reported metrics must always name the stage, never relabel pre-cap numbers as capped or vice versa

verification.delivery_contract: src/beer_models/delivery_current.py and its tests are out of this task write scope and still assert the pre-cap row (q1_topk_nonforced = 0.408 / 204 / 16); the capped row is the official submission and its numbers are the ones quoted in the audit-fix report

runtime_integration.rate_source: observed panel-weighted median high-grade fractions on the fixed full training panel; per-target k = round(rate * n_rows) at prediction time
runtime_integration.predict_path: scripts/current.py predict q1 -> beer_models.inference.run -> _official_grade_frame -> beer_models.q1_decision.runtime_decision (the same function used by this official table) then the deterministic parent/child cap
outputs_keep: estimated_grade_0_6 becomes the official top-k grade
grade_legacy_integer_median keeps the legacy ET integer median
estimated_grades_primary47.csv / estimated_grades_all52.csv are rebuilt from the official grades
runtime_integration.consistency_proof: experiments/lead_review/q1/runtime_check.py trains a real bundle, runs inference.run on 1.csv and asserts official == runtime_decision == topk+cap (max |diff| 0.0), the stored implementation_sha256 equals the current module hash, and 0 parent violations
